in_arabic.name: كليم

data.cultural_impact: The name "Kalim" has historical and cultural significance in the Muslim world. It was used by several significant figures in Islamic history, such as Kalim ibn Zidan, a notable theologian and scholar, and Kalimullah Shah, a Sufi saint. In the wider Muslim community, the name is often given to children as a sign of respect for the power of speech and communication, which holds great importance in Islamic teachings.
data.spiritual_significance: From a religious perspective, "Kalim" embodies the idea of divine communication between God and His creation. The name is associated with the Quranic phrase "Al-Kalimu-l-Lammiyy" - the All-Glorious Quran, emphasizing the sacredness and power of speech and expression. Additionally, the name can be linked to the concept of the "secret name of God" in Sufism, where it is said that uttering the name of God with pure intention can bring spiritual enlightenment and closeness to the Divine.
